answer: In a marketplace where agents buy velvet or ship trellis kits across the ocean, voting power can equal the number of tokens locked for 30 days. Splitting 1,000 locked tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 1,000 votes, so fake accounts add no influence. To gain more voting power, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital and forgoing its use elsewhere throughout the lock period.
